For example, `SELECT 'left | right' AS preview` produces this Desktop table: ```text preview -------------------- left | right 1 row(s) ``` The CLI reports `{"columns":["preview"],"rows":[{"preview":"left"}],"row_count":1}` and drops ` | right`. body_excerpt: `omi_cli.config.save()` unconditionally chmods `config.path.parent` to `0700`, including an existing shared directory selected through `OMI_CONFIG`. In a temporary POSIX test directory initially set to `0750`, saving a config changes the directory to `0700`; `0775` and setgid `02770` are also overwritten. The same mutation happens when TOML serialization subsequently fails, and when the parent is a symlink to another directory. This changes access to unrelated files in the parent, not just the credential file. I reproduced this with the real `config.py` and `_secure_file.py` modules, verified against Git blobs `5fc313e32ca7cf152fa4edbd98f844e78f669d65` and `104132409d084399a4f3855f6689320af21c5091`, using actual Tomli-W 1.2.0 on Linux/Python 3.13.5. Only temporary directories and synthetic credentials were used. Minimal reproduction after installing the Python CLI dependencies: ```python import stat from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from omi_cli import config as cfg with TemporaryDirectory() as directory: shared = Path(directory) / "shared" shared.mkdir() shared.chmod(0o750) cfg.save(cfg.Config(path=shared / "omi.toml")) print(oct(stat.S_IMODE(shared.stat().st_mode))) # actual: 0o700 print(oct(stat.S_IMODE((shared / "omi.toml").stat().st_mode))) # 0o600 ``` Expected: preserve permissions on an existing user-selected parent, while retaining owner-only permissions on the credential file and newly created config directory. body_excerpt: # Appendix: security research findings, vendor evaluations and sources This is the research appendix to the security program issue. It holds the material that would have buried the roadmap: the per-lane findings, the tool and vendor comparisons, the MCP server evaluation, the compliance calendar, and the sources. Nothing here is a task — every actionable item was promoted into the main issue. Findings the agents asserted but that I could not verify are marked as such, because an unverified claim in a security document is worse than no claim. ## How this was produced Seven agents ran in parallel on 2026-09-07. Six did web research against primary sources with a requirement to cite a URL for every claim and to flag anything unverifiable: one each on Next.js and Netlify, Supabase and Postgres, Better Auth, AI and MCP security, the AppSec program and toolchain, and Indian compliance. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia. We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown.
